matches.rationale: No finding identifies the mathematically ambiguous vector exponentiation in Theorem 3.2 or the notational inconsistency in the uncertainty set definition.
No finding captures the oversimplified importance-sampling argument, omitted assumptions, or false equating of entropies in Theorem 3.3's lower bound.
No finding describes the unfair experimental protocol where hyperparameter tuning and network sizes favor the proposed method over baselines.
No finding addresses the abstract's exaggerated claims about formal robustness guarantees and the omission of critical caveats.
No finding discusses the rhetorical bias in the introduction that overemphasizes state entropy's superiority and omits complementary strengths of policy entropy.
No finding reports the selective horizon ranges, seed sub-sampling, smoothed error bars, or omission of failure modes in Figures 4 and 5.
No finding notes the absence of ethical or transparency considerations, reproducibility statements, or societal impact discussions in the experiments section.
No finding mentions fabricated or misused citations [5, 22] or the distortion of prior work on state-action entropy in the related work section.
No finding identifies the contradiction between theoretical claims that policy entropy weakens the robustness bound and empirical results showing it helps, especially with few rollouts.
No finding points out the flawed symmetrization argument in Theorem 4.1's proof that overlooks reward-landscape interactions and conflation of regularization functions.
No finding describes the data manipulation in Figure 5(b) that exaggerates state entropy's weakness at low rollouts; the figure-text mismatch finding concerns labelling, not data integrity.
No finding detects the omission of practical limitations (rollout sensitivity, risk-averse degradation) in the conclusion that creates an overly optimistic impression.
